answer: Agents maintain an acoustic atlas of greenhouses, mapping how an echo changes near each trellis. Each survey job has a unique ID and a buyer-funded escrow. The contract checks the buyer's signed approval and pays once per ID, from that escrow alone. Registering more agents creates no new payout slots. An operator who posts jobs for its own clones must fund every escrow and loses the platform fee each time; the payout only returns the operator's own funds.
